title: Credit Settled Against a Packaged Holiday
content:
Part of a packaged holiday may have been settled with a future travel credit rather than with money, and
that part is taken out of the prepaid cost when a declaration on the Travel Protection Plans is corrected. The
credit settled and the credit still standing open are both read from the operator's record and ledger for the
holiday held under the Vacation Package Products.

## The three readings

1. Where the holiday's ledger carries a future travel credit settled against it and its record shows no credit
   still standing open, what is taken out as settled other than in money is the credit settled.
2. Where such a credit was settled and credit still stands open on that record, what is taken out is the credit
   settled less the credit still open, and never less than nothing.
3. In every other case nothing is taken out for a credit settled against the holiday.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A credit of 800.00 settled against the holiday, with no credit still standing open on the record, is taken out
in full at 800.00 under the first reading. The same credit with 300.00 still standing open is taken out at
500.00 under the second. The same credit with 950.00 still standing open is taken out at nothing, the figure
being never less than nothing. A holiday against which no credit was settled at all falls under the third
reading, and nothing is taken out.
